messages:
maria: Hey - nightly canary deploy started failing ~03:12 UTC. Runner logs show 401 from token exchange: 'invalid_grant'. Anyone seen this pattern?
joel: Noticed similar earlier today on a subset of repos, usually affects jobs that pull model bundles. Can you paste the error snippet?
maria: Sure - log tail:
```
2026-02-12T03:12:45Z ERROR fetcher: bundle fetch failed
status=401 err="invalid_grant: audience mismatch"
expected_aud=ci.read.redwood.internal got=redwood-hosted
job=canary/model-publish run=nightly-42
```
joel: audience mismatch is classic OIDC aud claim problem. Which runner type is this (gha, gitlab, self-hosted)?
maria: GitHub Actions self-hosted runners in our dedicated pool (ci-runner). Only the canary matrix is failing, prod jobs fine.
ci-runner: I can repro locally - when I request short-lived SA token from STS the token response has aud=repo:myorg/myrepo:ref:refs/heads/main unless you pass audience param to impersonation API.
infra-bot: Config dump for runner pool ci-canary:
```
provider: github
workload_identity: enabled
oidc_audience: "" # blank
impersonation: service-account:ci-deploy@redwood-internal.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
joel: Looks like the runner config never set oidc_audience, so STS returns repo-scoped aud, then our token exchange expects ci.read.* audience and rejects. That explains why only canary jobs (repo moved during migration) see it.
sre-lead: Agreed. Quick mitigation: set oidc_audience to ci.read.redwood.internal for the pool and restart runner service. That should produce tokens with the expected aud. Also add a fallback in fetcher to log the aud claim and surface alerts when aud != expected.
maria: Applied the change to ci-canary pool and restarted one runner. Re-ran the failing job and it passed.
joel: Nice. Can you add the exact repro steps so we can run a smoke test?
maria: Repro steps I used:
1) On self-hosted runner, request OIDC token from metadata endpoint (GHA env) without audience -> observe aud=repo:...
2) Call STS impersonation: `gcloud iam service-accounts impersonate --audiences=ci.read.redwood.internal` -> token has aud=ci.read.redwood.internal
3) Run `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://internal-api.redwood/v1/bundles` -> 200 if aud matches, 401 if mismatch
(Exact commands pasted to the infra runbook)

sre-lead: Follow-ups: 1) Patch runner bootstrap to require oidc_audience in pool config (done) 2) Add alert on token_aud_mismatch metric + note in deploy checklist 3) Update least-privilege guidance: use audience-restricted tokens and limit scopes to `storage.objects.get` not broad IAM roles.
joel: I'll open a PR for the bootstrap check and add a small unit test that simulates STS aud variations.
infra-bot: ticket created: INF-2026 - "OIDC audience enforcement and alerting for self-hosted runners" assigned to joel, sre-lead, maria. ETA 48h. :white_check_mark: 
maria: Thanks team. Leaving this thread with the workaround documented in the runbook and a follow-up on rotation cadence for the CI SA. :thumbsup:
joel: Also added a short-lived smoke job in nightly CI to catch regressions. :rocket:
